rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via Kernel Streaming Device IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY Exploitation
id: 2ff912e8-159f-4789-a2ef-761292b32a23
status: experimental
description: Detects local user-mode processes sending crafted IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY requests to kernel streaming devices (MSKSSRV, ksthunk.sys, ks.sys) which is indicative of exploitation attempts for CVE-2024-35250 privilege escalation vulnerability.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2024/12/cisa-and-fbi-raise-alerts-on-exploited.html
    - https://devco.re/blog/2024/08/23/streaming-vulnerabilities-from-windows-kernel-proxying-to-kernel-part1-en/

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1211/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/001
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1211
    - attack.t1078.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY'
            - 'KSPROPERTY_TYPE_UNSERIALIZESET'
            - 'KSPROPSETID_DrmAudioStream'
            - 'KsSynchronousIoControlDevice'
            - 'CheckIrpForStackAdjustmentNative'
            - 'ExAllocatePoolWithTag'
        Image|endswith:

            - '\ksthunk.sys'
            - '\ks.sys'

level: high

pipeline.attack_summary: Attackers exploit CVE-2024-35250 in Microsoft Windows Kernel Streaming Service (MSKSSRV) to perform privilege escalation through crafted IOCTL_KS_PROPERTY requests. The vulnerability involves improper handling of RequestorMode in kernel streaming operations, allowing attackers to bypass security checks and execute arbitrary code with elevated privileges. This is achieved by leveraging double fetch vulnerabilities in UnserializePropertySet function and manipulating IRP structures to gain kernel-level access.

status: experimental
description: Detects execution of malware binaries such as events.exe, splitter.exe, bitsadmin.exe, and expand.exe which are indicative of the Chafer APT group's use of an AutoIt script to drop malware via FTP with hardcoded credentials.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/chafer-used-remexi-malware/89538/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'events.exe'
            - 'splitter.exe'
            - 'bitsadmin.exe'
            - 'expand.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software using these tools for legitimate purposes

id: 5e2a4f7d-8b3c-4f0a-a1d9-6e8c3a3b5f9e

    category: webserver

        cs-uri-query|contains: 'usersfiles'
        cs-method: POST
        sc-status: 200

id: b9f4e8d2-6a5c-4b6f-c7d3-2b1c4d5e6f7a

title: Scheduled Task Creation by Administrator with Malicious Payload
id: 2a9e3b4c-7f8d-4e5a-9c1b-6d8e2f4a7b9c
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task named '\Microsoft\StartListener' by administrator 'dadmin', which executes 'C:\Documents\listener.exe'. This behavior aligns with initial access and persistence techniques using scheduled tasks.
references:
    - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4698
    - https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/kapeka
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/006/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1053.005
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: security
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        - Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
        - OriginalFileName: schtasks.exe
    selection_cli:
        CommandLine|contains|windash: ' /create '
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Microsoft\StartListener'
            - 'C:\Documents\listener.exe'
    selection_user:
        User|endswith: 'dadmin'
    condition: all of selection_ *
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts creating scheduled tasks
level: high

description: Detects an unauthenticated attacker sending a crafted HTTP request with a malicious SESSID cookie value to the GlobalProtect login endpoint (/global-protect/login.esp), which triggers arbitrary file creation and subsequent command injection via the device telemetry feature. references:

author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03

    - attack.t1566.001
logsource:
    category: webserver

        cs-uri-stem|startswith: /global-protect/login.esp

    condition: selection

id: 5e0d9f3a-7b64-4d1c-b828-12a7e1f5c8a3

description: Detects the initial access phase of Atomic macOS Stealer where users are tricked into copying and pasting malicious commands into the macOS Terminal. This rule targets common patterns used in ClickFix-style attacks such as base64 decoding followed by bash execution.

    - https://hunt.io/blog/macos-clickfix-applescript-terminal-phishing

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1598/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:

    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1204.004
    - attack.t1598.003
    - attack.t1204.001

    - attack.t1204

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with unauthenticated access to Veeam Backup & Replication via TCP port 9401, followed by execution of PowerShell scripts through SQL shell commands. title: Initial Access via Unauthenticated Command Injection in Commvault
id: 3d5e0a7c-2f8b-4d9a-9b6e-1c4d8f2a1b3c
status: experimental
description: Detects an unauthenticated HTTP GET request to the vulnerable /commandcenter/RestServlet/Test/Echo/ endpoint with command injection payload using qlogin -cs argument injection, indicating initial access via CVE-2025-XXXX in Commvault.
references:
    - https://labs.watchtowr.com/guess-who-would-be-stupid-enough-to-rob-the-same-vault-twice-pre-auth-rce-chains-in-commvault/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1210/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-03
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.t1210
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-stem|startswith: '/commandcenter/RestServlet/Test/Echo/'
        cs-uri-query|contains: 'qlogin -cs'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts or monitoring tools using similar patterns
level: high

description: Detects exploitation of command injection vulnerability in Commvault by injecting -localadmin argument into qlogin command, enabling authentication bypass and credential access.

title: Execution via QCommand with XML Payload in Commvault
id: 31386ad2-d791-4991-bd3c-bb2bab417f4c
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of QCommand with XML payload that enables arbitrary command execution and remote code access in Commvault environment, following successful privilege escalation.
references:

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack begins with a spear-phishing email containing an MHTML document attachment that exploits CVE-2015-2545 to execute code and drop the TidePool malware. indicators.context: The new malware family named TidePool is being used in an ongoing attack campaign against Indian embassy personnel worldwide.

TidePool contains many capabilities common to most RATs. It allows the attacker to read, write and delete files and folders, and run commands over named pipes. TidePool gathers information about the victim's computer, base64 encodes the data, and sends it to the Command and Control (C2) server via HTTP, which matches capabilities of the BS2005 malware family used by the Ke3chang actor
The weaponized document sent in phishing emails triggers the vulnerability outlined in CVE-2015-2545, which was first made public in September 2015.

status: experimental

    product: windows

            - 'ESX Admins'

id: 5a7e8c9b-4d2f-4a3e-9b8c-7d6e5f4a3b2c

description: |
    This rule detects the initial access phase of an attack exploiting CVE-2020-10189 in ManageEngine Desktop Central.
    The attack involves sending an unauthenticated HTTP POST request to the /mdm/client/v1/mdmLogUploader endpoint
    with a serialized Java payload. The payload is typically sent using application/octet-stream content type and
    includes gadgets like CommonsBeanutils1. This rule focuses on the initial access vector where the attacker
    sends the malicious payload to trigger deserialization.
references:
    - https://www.fireeye.com/blog/threat-research/2020/03/apt41-initiates-global-intrusion-campaign-using-multiple-exploits.html

    category: webserver
